title: Integral determinant-one coordinate avoidance for curve pencils
statement:
Let $A$ be an infinite integral domain with fraction field $K$, put $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $\psi:Y\to\mathbf P^1_U$ be a finite surjective $U$-morphism. Assume $C=Y_K$ is a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $K$-curve of dimension one and $\psi_K$ is etale on a nonempty open of $C$. Let $M\subset C$ be a reduced finite etale closed subscheme. There exists a matrix $g\in\mathrm{SL}_2(A)$ such that, for $\varphi=g\circ\psi$, each of the three fibres of $\varphi_K$ above $0=[0:1]$, $1=[1:1]$, and $\infty=[1:0]$ is finite etale over $K$, and their union is reduced and disjoint from $M$. More precisely, if $V\subset C$ is any nonempty open on which $\psi_K$ is etale and $R=C\setminus V$, $g$ can be chosen with $g_K(\psi_K(R\cup|M|))\cap\{0,1,\infty\}=\varnothing$. Here $\mathrm{SL}_2(A)$ is the group of two-by-two matrices with entries in $A$ and determinant one, acting by homogeneous coordinates on $\mathbf P^1_U$. The morphism $\varphi$ remains finite and surjective, and preserves invariance under any group of $U$-automorphisms of $Y$ for which $\psi$ was invariant.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-base-change], [def-kun-projective], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. An integral domain has $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors; $|M|$ is the underlying closed subset.

proof.text: Fix the nonempty open $V$ in the more precise assertion and put $R=C\setminus V$. The scheme $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. It is irreducible and has dimension one. Any chain $Z_0\subsetneq Z_1$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $R$ would extend to $Z_0\subsetneq Z_1\subsetneq C$, contrary to this dimension. Thus $\dim R\le0$ (including $R=\varnothing$). Schemes are $T_0$, so [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] shows that $R$ is finite. Since $M$ is finite over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$, it is affine by the definition of a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Its finite etale coordinate algebra is a finite product of finite separable fields by [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion]; in particular $|M|$ is finite. Consequently $B=\psi_K(R\cup|M|)$ is a finite set of scheme points of $\mathbf P^1_K$.

proof.text:
For each $p\in B$, take its residue-field-valued point and write its homogeneous coordinates as $[x_p:y_p]$ over $\kappa(p)$, with $(x_p,y_p)
e(0,0)$. The field map $K	o\kappa(p)$ is injective by [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension], so distinct elements of $A\subset K$ remain distinct in $\kappa(p)$. If $y_p=0$, then $x_p+a y_p
e0$ for every $a\in A$. Otherwise $x_p+a y_p=0$ excludes at most one $a\in A$: subtracting two such equations gives $(a-a\prime)y_p=0$. Finitely many points therefore exclude finitely many elements. Choose $a\in A$ outside them, using the infinitude of $A$, and put $X_p=x_p+a y_p
e0$. This is just multiplication by the upper elementary matrix $u(a)$ with diagonal entries $1$, upper-right entry $a$ and lower-left entry $0$.

source.place: §3.4, printed p.606, final paragraph: changing coordinates to avoid 0,1,infinity; explicit two-transvection argument by Q31 (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online).

proof.text: With $a$ fixed, each equation $y_p+bX_p=0$ and each equation $y_p+bX_p=X_p$ excludes at most one $b\in A$, since $X_p\ne0$ and $A\to\kappa(p)$ is injective. Choose $b\in A$ avoiding these finitely many values. Set $g=l(b)u(a)$, where $l(b)$ has diagonal entries $1$, upper-right entry $0$ and lower-left entry $b$. Thus $g_{00}=1$, $g_{01}=a$, $g_{10}=b$ and $g_{11}=1+ab$. Its determinant is $1+ab-ab=1$, and it sends $[x_p:y_p]$ to $[X_p:y_p+bX_p]$. Both coordinates are nonzero and unequal. Hence this point is neither $0=[0:1]$, nor $\infty=[1:0]$, nor $1=[1:1]$. This proves the more precise avoidance assertion directly, including for nonrational or inseparable closed points; no choice of geometric lifts or separability of the bad points is required.

source.place: §3.4, printed p.606, final paragraph: changing coordinates to avoid 0,1,infinity; explicit two-transvection argument by Q31 (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online).

proof.text: The homogeneous-coordinate action in the statement gives a $U$-automorphism $g$ with inverse matrix whose entries in row order are $1+ab,-a,-b,1$: the two products are the identity. Put $\varphi=g\circ\psi$. This morphism is finite directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: for every affine open $W$ in the target, $g^{-1}W$ is affine and isomorphic to $W$, and the finite coordinate algebra of $\psi^{-1}(g^{-1}W)$ over $\mathcal O(g^{-1}W)$ stays finite after this ring isomorphism. Surjectivity follows because $g$ is bijective and $\psi$ is surjective. For any automorphism $h$ of $Y$ with $\psi h=\psi$, associativity gives $\varphi h=g\psi h=g\psi=\varphi$, establishing the entire invariance clause over $U$, not just over $K$.

source.place: §3.4, printed p.606, final paragraph: changing coordinates to avoid 0,1,infinity; explicit two-transvection argument by Q31 (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online).

proof.text: For $t\in\{0,1,\infty\}$ let $q_t=g_K^{-1}(t)$, a $K$-rational point. The scheme fibre $F_t$ of $\varphi_K$ over $t$ is canonically the scheme fibre of $\psi_K$ over $q_t$ (compose the defining pullback square with the isomorphism $g_K$). It is finite over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], applied first to $\psi$ along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$ and then to its fibre. Step 3 implies that no point of $F_t$ lies in $R$ or $|M|$. Thus the inverse image of the open $V$ in $F_t$ is the whole scheme; by the open-subscheme meaning of [def-weil-open-immersion] its map to $C$ factors through $V$. Consequently $F_t=V\times_{\mathbf P^1_K,q_t}\operatorname{Spec}K$ as schemes. The morphism $V\to\mathbf P^1_K$ is etale by the chosen hypothesis on $V$, so clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] proves that $F_t\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is etale.

source.place: §3.4, printed p.606, final paragraph: changing coordinates to avoid 0,1,infinity; explicit two-transvection argument by Q31 (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online).

proof.text: Each $F_t$ is affine and finite etale over $K$, so [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion] identifies its coordinate ring with a finite product of finite separable fields. Such a product has no nonzero nilpotent, hence each $F_t$ is reduced. The three fibres are pairwise disjoint closed subschemes, since their images are three distinct closed points of $\mathbf P^1_K$. Their scheme-theoretic union is locally one of the $F_t$: near a point of one fibre remove the other two closed fibres. It is therefore reduced, and its underlying set is disjoint from $|M|$ by Step 5, which also makes its intersection with $M$ the empty scheme. Choosing any one nonempty etale open supplies the initial existence assertion; the construction already worked for every specified such $V$.
